Description:
[b]Rome Expanded Submod[/b] is a gameplay and balance add-on for Rome Expanded.

[b]Military Building Conversion[/b]

• All player-controlled factions can convert captured barracks, stables and missile ranges into their own military buildings instead of demolishing and rebuilding them.

• Conversion is available for all four tiers of each military branch and preserves the equivalent building tier.

[b]Balance Changes[/b]

• Building weapon upgrades have been replaced with armour, morale and law bonuses. Weapon upgrades doubled weapon lethality instead of merely adding +1 attack, causing battles to end much too quickly.

• The player's capital receives a 20% taxable-income bonus. It supports the difficult early campaign without scaling across the whole empire, so its relative impact decreases as expansion makes the late game easier.

• Roman infantry is more expensive to recruit and maintain.

• Barbarian infantry upkeep has been reduced by 40%, compensating for barbarian factions' technological disadvantage compared with civilised factions.

• Cavalry recruitment and upkeep costs have been substantially increased.

• Siege engines now cost 300 denarii per turn in upkeep.

• Battering rams no longer catch fire like matchsticks. Siege towers now catch fire 40% faster and can be burned down by archers using flaming arrows.

• Building construction times are capped at three turns.

• Mercenary replenishment is slower.

• Long-campaign victory requirements have been reduced.

• Many factions now begin the campaign with 9,999 denarii instead of 5,000, giving them more resources for early recruitment and construction.

• The Colossus of Rhodes' faction-wide +40% trade bonus has been neutralised because it was excessively overpowered and unbalanced the campaign.

• WIP — the phalanx formation is being nerfed: in its current overpowered state, a single unit can destroy up to 500 enemy troops.

[b]Religion and Conversion[/b]

• Governor buildings no longer provide passive religious conversion. This makes conversion a deliberate, gradual part of expansion rather than an automatic effect of settlement administration.

• Build a temple in conquered settlements and station generals there: generals help spread your state religion, much like priests.

• Nearby settlements of your religion support conversion. Each adjacent settlement adds a 5% conversion bonus, up to 15% from three such neighbours.

[b]Campaign Improvements[/b]

• Fleet movement points increased from 100% to 300%. Naval raids and coastal landings have never been so easy ) 

• At campaign start, players can enable early Marian reforms. When enabled, the reforms begin once the Roman factions collectively control 10 large cities or larger settlements. When disabled, the standard requirement of five huge cities remains. The reforms will still trigger automatically after turn 325.

• Fixed an issue that could prevent minor factions from recruiting units in settlements affected by the poverty hidden resource.

• Fixed an issue that could cause AI-controlled factions to get stuck at the first settlement level, preventing further settlement upgrades.

[b]Requirements[/b]
Requires Rome Expanded.
